mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about the difference between mechanical and electromagnetic waves?

options.A: Electromagnetic waves can travel through vacuum, while mechanical waves require a material medium.
options.B: Mechanical waves can travel through vacuum because they do not need a medium.
options.C: Both mechanical and electromagnetic waves transfer energy without permanent transport of matter.
options.D: The speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum is approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s, which is much higher than typical speeds of mechanical waves in air.

mcqs.answer: Mechanical waves can travel through vacuum because they do not need a medium.
mcqs.explanation: Mechanical waves need a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate; they cannot travel through vacuum. Option B states the opposite, making it the incorrect statement. Options A, C, and D correctly describe the differences: mechanical waves need a medium, EM waves do not, both transfer energy without net matter transport, and EM waves travel at the speed of light, which is far greater than typical mechanical wave speeds.

mcqs.question: In a transverse wave traveling along a stretched string, the direction of the particle displacement is:

options.A: Parallel to the direction of wave propagation
options.B: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
options.C: Circular around the axis of propagation
options.D: Random, with no fixed relation to the propagation direction

mcqs.answer: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
mcqs.explanation: In a transverse wave, particles of the medium move at right angles (perpendicular) to the direction in which the wave travels. This is why a string vibrates up and down while the wave moves horizontally. Option B correctly captures this relationship; the other options describe longitudinal motion, circular polarization, or no specific pattern, which are not characteristics of a simple transverse wave on a string.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares longitudinal and transverse waves?

options.A: In longitudinal waves, particle displacement is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation, whereas in transverse waves it is parallel.
options.B: Both longitudinal and transverse waves have particle displacement parallel to the direction of propagation.
options.C: In longitudinal waves, particle displacement is parallel to the direction of wave propagation, whereas in transverse waves it is perpendicular.
options.D: Longitudinal waves can exist only in solids, while transverse waves can exist only in fluids.

mcqs.answer: In longitudinal waves, particle displacement is parallel to the direction of wave propagation, whereas in transverse waves it is perpendicular.
mcqs.explanation: The defining difference is the orientation of particle motion relative to wave travel. Longitudinal waves (e.g., sound in air) involve compressions and rarefactions along the direction of travel, while transverse waves (e.g., waves on a string) involve motion at right angles to travel. Option C states this correctly. Option A reverses the relationship, B incorrectly claims both are parallel, and D misstates the media in which each type can exist.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines each of the listed wave parameters?

options.A: Wavelength is the number of oscillations per second; frequency is the distance between successive crests; amplitude is the maximum displacement from equilibrium; period is the time taken for one complete oscillation.
options.B: Wavelength is the distance between successive points that are in phase; frequency is the number of oscillations per second; amplitude is the maximum displacement from equilibrium; period is the time taken for one complete oscillation.
options.C: Wavelength is the time taken for one oscillation; frequency is the distance between successive crests; amplitude is the speed of the wave; period is the number of oscillations per second.
options.D: Wavelength is the maximum speed of particles; frequency is the distance between successive nodes; amplitude is the time for one cycle; period is the distance between successive crests.

mcqs.answer: Wavelength is the distance between successive points that are in phase; frequency is the number of oscillations per second; amplitude is the maximum displacement from equilibrium; period is the time taken for one complete oscillation.
mcqs.explanation: Option B accurately defines all four parameters: • Wavelength (λ) – the spatial distance between two consecutive points in the same phase (e.g., crest to crest). • Frequency (f) – how many complete cycles occur per second (Hz). • Amplitude – the greatest displacement of the medium from its equilibrium position. • Period (T) – the time required for one full cycle, equal to 1/f. The other options mix up definitions, assigning incorrect meanings to the terms.
